source_grounding.call_chain_traced: REST GET /collections/{name} -> toc/mod.rs:383 get_collection (collections map lookup; absent -> StorageError::not_found "Collection `X` doesn't exist!" -> the clean 404) -> collection_ops.rs:329 Collection::info -> shard_holder select -> read_ops.rs:201-207 ShardReplicaSet::info(local_only=false) -> execute_read_operation.rs:23 execute_read_operation(.., false) -> execute_cluster_read_operation(required=1). There, operations = local_operation ONLY IF peer_is_readable(this_peer_id), chained with readable remotes; on this single-node deployment remotes is always empty, so when the local peer state is not readable — removed by remove_local (mod.rs:652-656) during the drop leg, or Initializing/Listener (replica_set_state.rs:156-168) during the create leg — the operations stream is EMPTY, pending_operations.next() returns None immediately (execute_read_operation.rs:283-285 -> break), leaving responses=0 and errors=0, which fails the required>=1 check and formats '0 of 0 read operations failed' -> CollectionError::service_error -> StorageError 'Service internal error: ...' -> HTTP 500. The describe path via execute_read_operation skips even the 'does not have enough active replicas' pre-check that exists on the execute_and_resolve_read_operation path (lines 96-102), which itself would also return a 500-class service error. Comparative confirmation: the exists endpoint is a pure map contains_key (collections_ops.rs:36-38) and never enters the replica-set read — matching its 0-non-200 record under the identical churn (output_state_collections_exists_005.log).
source_grounding.note: No graceful-degradation handling exists for the no-readable-replica-yet window on the describe path: the code neither retries, nor falls back, nor maps the empty-operations case to a 404/200 — it fabricates a vacuous error message ('0 of 0 read operations failed': zero operations attempted, zero failed) and returns service_error while the collection is still resolvable in the map (so the clean 404 branch is not reached either). No comment/docstring marks this intentional; the unrelated 'does not have enough active replicas' sibling check shows awareness of replica-availability failures but still chooses a 500-class service error. by_design_in_source is therefore not available (no explicit intent evidence).
